findings.highlight: She's a world-class Japanese born in Japan, and after she changed her main site of activity to Europe, she had not come back to her home country even once for years on end.
findings.evidenceJa: 活動拠点をヨーロッパに移してから、数年に一度くらいしか帰国しない、日本が生んだ世界的ピアニスト。
findings.explanation: The source calls Youko a world-famous pianist produced by Japan who, since moving her professional base to Europe, returns home only about once every few years. The translation turns her profession into the nonsensical 'world-class Japanese,' then changes intermittent visits into no return for years on end.
findings.japanese:
活動拠点をヨーロッパに移してから、
数年に一度くらいしか帰国しない、
日本が生んだ世界的ピアニスト。
findings.todokanai: She's a world-class Japanese born in Japan, and after she changed her main site of activity to Europe, she had not come back to her home country even once for years on end.

findings.highlight: They have quite the competition this time.
findings.evidenceJa: なんでもあれに対抗してるんだと
findings.explanation: Hamada says Youko's New Year's concert is apparently intended to compete with artists' overnight New Year's Eve live shows. The translation instead says an unspecified 'they' face strong competition, reversing who is challenging whom.
findings.japanese:
「大晦日に年越しライブやるアーティストいるだろ。
なんでもあれに対抗してるんだと」
findings.todokanai: "Aren't there plenty of artists out there that do cross-year concerts on New Year's Eve? They have quite the competition this time."

findings.highlight: I heard she was going to play Number 9 too. I guess she found some orchestra to perform with her
findings.evidenceJa: 第九も弾くんだとさ。どっかの交響楽団にも張り合ってるんだな
findings.explanation: 第九 is Beethoven's Ninth Symphony, not an item called 'Number 9.' Hamada then jokes that Youko is even taking on some symphony orchestra as a rival; the translation invents an orchestra performing with her and erases the second competitive comparison.
findings.japanese:
「聞いた話だと、第九も弾くんだとさ。
どっかの交響楽団にも張り合ってるんだな…
なんつ～か、若いよなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "I heard she was going to play Number 9 too. I guess she found some orchestra to perform with her… How should I put it, she's still so young and full of life, huh?"

findings.highlight: Apparently, she got a call directly from the chief editor over at Ensemble.
findings.evidenceJa: 昨夜、本人からアンサンブルの編集長に直接連絡があったそうで
findings.explanation: Matsuoka says that last night Youko herself directly contacted Ensemble's editor-in-chief, which is why the special instruction reached Mari and then this office. The translation instead has Mari receiving a call from that editor, omitting Youko's direct intervention and reversing the stated call direction.
findings.japanese:
「さっきの電話、麻理さんからだったんですよ。
昨夜、本人からアンサンブルの編集長に
直接連絡があったそうで」
findings.todokanai: "That call just now was from Mari-san. Apparently, she got a call directly from the chief editor over at Ensemble."
